title: I Spy the Letter Ll — Visual Scanning Activity (Twinkl)

overview.description: Single-page 'I Spy' letter identification worksheet. Top: large Ll model (bold L + grey traceable L on writing lines). Center: lion illustration. Scattered across the page: ~30 circled letters in various fonts/cases — uppercase L, lowercase l, and similar-looking distractors (I, i, E, F, g). Child finds and marks all instances of L and l among the look-alike distractors.

visualScanningGame.description: 'I Spy' framing turns letter identification into a search game. The child hunts for target letters among visually similar distractors. The distractors are carefully chosen: I/i (vertical line confusion), E/F (similar shapes), g (lowercase curve confusion).
visualScanningGame.value: Letter discrimination — the child must distinguish L from I (both have vertical lines), which is one of the most common early reading confusions.

themedCenterImage.description: A lion (L word) illustration in the center of the page. The letter-themed animal provides: (1) a visual anchor, (2) an initial-sound connection (L = lion), (3) a coloring opportunity.
themedCenterImage.value: Multi-purpose: letter association + coloring break + visual interest.

modelAndPractice.description: Top of page: large bold Ll model on writing lines + grey traceable version. The child sees the target letter in its correct form before hunting for it below.
modelAndPractice.value: Reference model always visible. The child can look up when unsure.

gaps.name: i-spy-letter-page
gaps.description: A single-page letter identification game: large letter model at top (bold + traceable), themed illustration in center (animal starting with target letter = coloring opportunity), ~30 circled letters scattered around the page (mix of target + visually similar distractors). Child circles/dabs all instances of the target letter. Generatable for any letter. Distractors should be intelligently chosen based on common confusions (b/d, p/q, l/I, m/n).

notes: Lightweight single-page drop. The 'I Spy' format is a new game mechanic for letter identification — different from the Habitat Schoolhouse approach (color/circle all uppercase letters on a page) because it specifically includes VISUALLY SIMILAR distractors. The chosen distractors for L (I, i, E, F, g) are pedagogically intentional — they test the specific confusions that matter for this letter.
